description: The Office of Congressman Greg Casar (TX-35) is seeking a candidate for one paid internship during the Fall 2026 term. This internship is full-time and in-person in the Washington DC office. The Fall 2026 internship will run from September 1 to December 17. Interns are paid $18.40/hour at the close of each month. Fall internships are 40 hours/week within the hours of 9 am-6 pm, Monday through Friday. Applications are due by Friday, August 21, 12PM ET.
responsibilities: Assisting staff with events, meetings, communications tasks
qualifications: Interns must be at least 18 years of age
Texas ties, district ties, and Spanish language fluency are preferred but not required
Employees of the House of Representatives must be Legal Permanent Residents or US Citizens
Demonstrate an interest in politics, policy, and/or public service
Possess a professional demeanor and an upbeat disposition while interacting with visitors, constituents, and staff members in a fast-paced, highly dynamic environment
Possess effective skills for verbal and written communications
Possess effective teamwork skills, flexibility, willingness to learn new skills, and the ability to support the needs of multiple team members and leaders in the office
Possess time management skills including the ability to prioritize and track work status
how_to_apply: Interested applicants should fill out the application form. Candidates are encouraged to describe in their cover letter how their experience translates to the role and needs of the office. Application deadline is Friday, August 21, 2026 at 12PM ET. Due to the large volume of applicants, only applicants selected for interviews will be contacted.
equal_opportunity: The Office of Congressman Greg Casar is an equal opportunity employer; we do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, military status, parental status, marital status, sexual orientation, or any other factor or basis prohibited by applicable federal law. Applicants with disabilities who require a reasonable accommodation to participate in the application or hiring processes are encouraged to request an accommodation at any time during those processes.

description: Law clerks will have the opportunity to work with the Committee's policy, oversight, and investigative teams, conducting legal and policy research, reviewing documents, and preparing materials for hearings, markups, and other Committee activities. The fall clerkship period runs from September to December. Preference will be given to candidates who are available at least three days per week. This is a paid position, and the Committee is happy to work with applicants seeking academic credit.
responsibilities: Prepare materials for hearings, markups, and other Committee activities
Work with the Committee's policy, oversight, and investigative teams
qualifications: Current law students
Strong research and writing skills
Enthusiastic about the Committee's mission to protect the homeland and strengthen national security
Available at least three days per week (preferred)
how_to_apply: Submit a resume, brief cover letter, and writing sample to CHSJobs@mail.house.gov with the subject line "Fall Law Clerkship." Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.

description: Representative Seth Magaziner (RI-02) seeks part-time, paid Fall 2026 interns for his Warwick, Rhode Island office, to start at the beginning of September and go until end of December. Duties include providing a welcoming environment and positive first impression of the Member office to constituents, visitors, and other VIPs; answering incoming calls with poise, professionalism, and promptness; assisting Member and key staff with logistical and administrative duties; receiving and logging input from constituents on policy matters; conducting research and drafting correspondence and memoranda; assisting with planning and execution of Member's public outreach at local events; and accompanying district staff to public forums, meetings, and events as a representative to the Member.
responsibilities: Provides a welcoming environment and positive first impression of the Member office to constituents, visitors, and other VIPs
Answers incoming calls with poise, professionalism, and promptness
Assists Member and key staff (e.g. Staff Assistant, Press Assistant, Constituent Services Team) with logistical and administrative duties
Receives and logs input from constituents on policy matters for the Member office's consideration and response
Conducts research, and drafts correspondence and memoranda
Assists with planning and execution of Member's public outreach at local events
Accompanies district staff to public forums, meetings, and events as a representative to the Member
qualifications: Strong interpersonal and communication skills
Professional demeanor and ability to interact with constituents and VIPs
Research and writing abilities for drafting correspondence and memoranda
Organizational skills for logistical and administrative duties
Interest in public service and community outreach

description: The House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform Democratic Staff seeks a motivated and reliable Video Production Intern this fall. Interns will be responsible for helping with clipping streams of sessions, editing and captioning videos, helping with shoots, scripting content and other administrative tasks as assigned. Successful candidates will possess extreme familiarity with Adobe Premiere Pro. Additional experiences with Adobe After Effects and Photoshop are a plus. Ability to work in a fast-paced, rapid response environment is a must. Candidates will be expected to work in-person in Washington, DC, with opportunities for remote work during Congressional recesses. Full-time candidates with diverse backgrounds and experiences are strongly encouraged to apply.
qualifications: Extreme familiarity with Adobe Premiere Pro
Additional experience with Adobe After Effects and Photoshop is a plus
Ability to work in a fast-paced, rapid response environment
Ability to work in-person in Washington, DC
how_to_apply: Send a resume, portfolio, and your availability this fall to ethan.cesar@mail.house.gov and OversightPress@mail.house.gov.

description: Congresswoman Doris Matsui, representing the 7th Congressional District of California, seeks interns for her Washington, D.C. office for the Fall 2026 term. The Press and Digital Intern will help communicate the Congresswoman's work through social media, graphics, photography, video, and other digital content. This position is well suited for a creative candidate who is interested in public service and eager to build communications experience in a congressional office. Washington DC interns may be asked to assist in researching legislation for the Member and legislative staff, attending briefings, hearings, and markups, and responding to constituent correspondence. Ties to California's 7th District are preferred, but not required. All applications are considered on a rolling basis.
responsibilities: Help communicate the Congresswoman's work through social media, graphics, photography, video, and other digital content
Assist in researching legislation for the Member and legislative staff
qualifications: Strong writing, editing, and social media skills to assist with time sensitive assignments
Basic familiarity with graphic design/video editing software
Strong writing, editing, and social media instincts
Familiarity with Canva, photography, video editing, or graphic design
An interest in digital marketing, audience engagement, or social media analytics
Strong media literacy, attention to detail, and sound judgment
An ability to listen closely, follow instructions, learn through observation and a willingness to try new approaches
Experience in a press or digital media role (including internships) preferred but not required
Ties to California's 7th District preferred but not required
how_to_apply: Visit the Internships page of Congresswoman Matsui's official website and complete the application form: https://matsui.house.gov/services/internships. A cover letter, resume, and 2 writing samples (1 writing sample & 1 graphic example preferred, but not required) must be submitted as part of the application.
equal_opportunity: This office is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate based on race, religion, disability, age, ethnicity, national origin, sex, gender, LGBTQ identification, family status, or military status.

description: Congresswoman Doris Matsui, representing the 7th Congressional District of California, seeks interns for her Washington, D.C. and District (Sacramento) offices for the Fall 2026 term. Interns will have a unique opportunity to learn about the legislative process firsthand and the many functions of a Congressional office. Intern responsibilities will vary but may include answering phones and data entry. Washington DC interns may be asked to assist in researching legislation for the Member and legislative staff, attending briefings, hearings, and markups; and answering constituent letters on various issues. Interns based in California may also be asked to assist on a variety of constituent casework or in-district projects, as needed. To apply, please visit the "Internships" page of Congresswomen Matsui's official website and complete the application form: https://matsui.house.gov/services/internships. As part of the application, a cover letter, resume, and 2 writing samples are required. Ties to California's 7th District are preferred, but not required. All applications are considered on a rolling basis. This office is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate based on race, religion, disability, age, ethnicity, national origin, sex, gender, LGBTQ identification, family status, or military status.
responsibilities: Researching legislation for the Member and legislative staff (Washington DC interns)
Attending briefings, hearings, and markups (Washington DC interns)
Answering constituent letters on various issues (Washington DC interns)
Assisting with in-district projects as needed (California-based interns)
qualifications: Ties to California's 7th District are preferred, but not required
Cover letter required
Resume required
Two writing samples required
how_to_apply: Visit the "Internships" page of Congresswoman Matsui's official website and complete the application form at https://matsui.house.gov/services/internships. A cover letter, resume, and 2 writing samples are required.
equal_opportunity: This office is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate based on race, religion, disability, age, ethnicity, national origin, sex, gender, LGBTQ identification, family status, or military status.
